title: P25: wider residual stream, narrower MLP: d_model 256 -> 320 (10 heads of 32), d_ff 1024 -> 576, parameter- and FLOP-matched, on the 107-claude Peri-LN Lean incumbent
description: P25: reallocate MLP parameters into residual width (d_model 320 with 10 heads of 32, MLP ratio 4.0 -> 1.8) at matched parameters (4.77M vs 4.80M) and matmul FLOPs, keeping six Peri-LN blocks and everything else fixed. A wider residual stream carries more simultaneous proof-state features (bound names, hypotheses, the current goal) and two more attention heads per layer, which should help the model keep long (>= 7 line) proofs consistent during expert iteration, while 103-claude suggests extra MLP capacity is not what limits RL.
hypothesis: At this budget capacity added as MLP width (103, -31) or sequential depth (102, 105, ~-35) hurt, while halving attention's unique parameters (106) cost no fit, so the MLP may be over-provisioned relative to the residual stream. With the model launch-bound and matmul FLOPs matched, a 320-wide residual stream keeps ~the same step count (predicted 3,100-3,300 vs 3,208-3,277) while giving each token 25% more feature dimensions and 10 instead of 8 retrieval heads; if long-proof failures come from tracking many names/hypotheses at once (unbound-name parse failures ~20% of samples), the wider stream should lower round-1 and eval parse failures and raise late-round RL solves.
expected_delta: -40 to +35 dev solves >= 7 vs 107-claude's 587.00 (central -5); pretraining 3,100-3,300 steps, final val loss 0.078-0.086; totals 1,850-2,200 s, under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input), custom MLP width
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN; unchanged from 107-claude)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 107-claude (P25, only edit): residual width d_model 256 -> 320 with 10 heads of 32 (head dim 32 and RoPE unchanged), MLP hidden 1024 -> 576 (ratio 4.0 -> 1.8). GPT(vocab, 6, 320, 10) is built, then model.blocks is replaced by six PeriLNBlock(320, 10, 576), whose __init__ now replaces the fork Block's fc1/fc2 with nn.Linear(320, 576) / nn.Linear(576, 320). Block forward, Peri-LN, depth, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f unchanged. Width persists into RL and eval
arch.n_params_detail: per block qkv 308,160 + proj 102,720 + fc1 184,896 + fc2 184,640 + 4 LayerNorms 2,560 = 782,976; x6 = 4,697,856; + emb 107x320 34,240 + head 34,240 + ln_f 640 = 4,766,976 (107-claude 4,800,000, -0.7%). Matmul params per token per block 4*320^2 + 2*320*576 = 778,240 vs 786,432 (-1.0%); attention-score FLOPs +25% (320 vs 256 q/k/v width). Checked on CPU with the pinned fork 51604b3 model.py and tokenizer (vocab 107)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 6, 320, 10) from the fork, replace blocks with PeriLNBlock(320, 10, 576) as in pretrain.py, then load state; a plain fork GPT would reject the shapes and ln_attn_out/ln_mlp_out keys. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: fork attn/cache code unchanged, one cache dict per model.blocks index. CPU check: 12 one-token cached steps vs full causal forward, max abs logit diff 1.4e-6

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged code: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D now 320: Q/K/V each (320,320) 1, proj 1, fc1 (576,320) sqrt(1.8)=1.34, fc2 1.34 (107-claude: 2 on fc1/fc2 at D 256), head (107,320) 1. Every Muon update still has element RMS lr/sqrt(D) scaled to a square DxD matrix; with D=320 that is ~1/17.9 instead of 1/16 times lr
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (960,320) split into Q/K/V of (320,320), proj (320,320), fc1 (576,320), fc2 (320,576)) plus head.weight (107,320)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,320,320); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. The (3D, D) shape test still matches only qkv (fc1 is (576,320))
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (960,320) split into Q/K/V of (320,320), proj (320,320), fc1 (576,320), fc2 (320,576)) plus head.weight (107,320)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Unchanged recipe from 107-claude: fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), element std 0.02); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0. Shapes differ, so RNG draws differ from 107-claude
